conventions.convention: Countable Choice is assumed; Hilbert inner products are linear in the first variable. The separable calculus requires a specified countable dense sequence; the arbitrary-Hilbert calculus instead assembles compatible finite-tuple Cayley subspaces.

Dyson products put the latest integration time on the left. Backward evolution uses signed oriented nested integrals; the exact truncation remainder has its residual propagator at the earliest forward integration time.

Strongly continuous bounded controls are integrated vectorwise. Their Dyson series converges in operator norm, but operator-valued norm-Bochner integrability and physical propagator invariance of D(H0) are not asserted.
The perturbation contour is counterclockwise and integrates (z-Hλ)^−1. Complex couplings give Riesz projections; orthogonality is asserted only for real couplings.

The base Fourier convention is exp(−2πix·ξ), so −Δ has multiplier 4π²|ξ|². Physical-momentum coordinates use exp(−ip·x) with normalization (2π)^−3/2. Gaussian complex powers use the principal logarithm.
Ordinary waves are limits of exp(itH)exp(−itH0). Position dilation is exp(−isD)ψ(x)=exp(−3s/2)ψ(exp(−s)x); P+ selects negative momentum-log Fourier frequencies and P− selects positive ones.
Airy connection errors are absolute envelope errors, including at oscillatory zeros. The decaying branch has terminal data at the positive endpoint; the growing branch has data at zero.

Stationary outgoing kernels are exp(ik|x−y|)/(4π|x−y|), k>0. The amplitude has coefficient −1/(4π), and the on-shell scattering operator is I+ik A_k/(2π). Nonradial potentials have rotational covariance rather than individual angular-channel preservation.

load_bearing.statement: Under Countable Choice, every densely defined self-adjoint operator on an arbitrary complex Hilbert space has a unique regular representing PVM, exact bounded and finite-valued unbounded Borel calculus, spectral support equal to its spectrum, and a strongly continuous unitary group with exact derivative domain D(A).

Under Countable Choice, a self-adjoint operator on a complex Hilbert space with a specified norm-dense sequence has a unique regular representing PVM, exact square-integrability domain and Borel calculus, and exp(itA) with strong derivative iAh exactly for h∈D(A).

Under Countable Choice, a self-adjoint family A(t) with common dense Hilbert domain Y continuously embedded in H and A∈C¹([0,T];B(Y,H)) has a unique unitary strong propagator preserving Y, with joint Y continuity, uniform domain bounds and both endpoint equations.

For a bounded norm-continuous self-adjoint family on an arbitrary complex Hilbert space, the oriented Dyson iterates satisfy ||U_n(t,s)||≤(K|t−s|)^n/n! and sum uniformly in operator norm to the unique unitary two-time propagator, with cocycle, inverse and both endpoint derivatives.

For the stated C⁵ single-simple-turning-point Liouville equation, the Airy terminal-data solutions obey value and derivative envelope errors controlled by exp(ε_h)−1, where ε_h=Ch∫|R(v)|/√(|v|+h^(2/3))dv≤C′h; their normalized branches give the sine/cosine connection with absolute matching errors.

For smooth free-energy cutoffs supported strictly inside (a²,b²), localized outgoing and incoming free propagation has operator-norm bounds C_N|t|(1+|t|)^−N in the matching time directions; the opposite-time projected evolutions tend strongly to zero.

For real bounded compactly supported V, VR_H0(i) is compact, (Ω±−I)f(H0)P± is compact for f∈C_c(R) with f(0)=0, and f(H)−f(H0) is compact for f∈C_0(R). A specified resonant square well makes the outgoing defect noncompact whenever f(0)≠0.
For real bounded compactly supported V in three dimensions, each ordinary wave operator individually has range H_ac(H)=H_c(H), H_sc(H)={0}, and S=Ω+*Ω− is unitary and commutes with the free group.

For real bounded V supported in B_R and every k>0, the compact outgoing operator K_k on L²(B_R) has I+K_k boundedly invertible, with norm-continuous uniformly bounded inverses on compact positive wave-number intervals and a complex neighborhood thereof.

concerns.concern: Proof 3.1 asserts H² approximation by smooth functions supported away from zero. The declared smooth-density supplier proves L² density only, and boundedness of the weights alone does not upgrade it to H² density. The conclusion is recoverable immediately by mollifying the compactly supported H² function with radii smaller than its distance from zero, or by citing the opened W^{k,p} smooth-density corollary and retaining annular support.

Verification F2 says its local uniqueness argument avoids 'the defective generic Dyson ordering'. The current norm-Dyson supplier explicitly has the corrected latest-time-left ordering. This historical wording should identify a former version rather than imply a defect in the current supplier.

alerts.finding: Facts F3 first defines η_+:=ζ(ξ0+s0), the positive endpoint, then writes 'φ_h(η)=2(η_+)^{3/2}/(3h)'. The cited supplier instead uses the positive part of the variable η. These share the same notation here: read literally with the preceding endpoint definition, the exponent is constant and the quoted envelopes are not the supplier's envelopes. Write max(η,0), or explicitly distinguish the positive-part notation from the endpoint.

seams_checked.note: Uses the concrete CC L²-kernel calculus and finite-block angular-radial unitary identity. The stronger Coulomb endpoint and spectral results are reconstructed locally rather than silently imported with stronger choice assumptions.
The complex Gaussian supplier is used on Re z>0 with its principal branch; oscillatory boundary limits are justified locally.
Pauli algebra, sphere ONB, associated Legendre functions and finite-span angular eigenidentities retain their normalization and domains.
Regular IVP/Picard-series content is used; holomorphic radial continuation is also derived locally, without treating a weaker real-parameter result as a complex theorem.
The exact diagonal oscillator and closed ladder domains are preserved. Maximal Q/P domains, square operators and Weyl invariance are established locally.
The examples use the stated two-by-two Pauli matrices and their finite algebra.

Perturbation radii, reduced inverse, remainder constants and WKB scaling are faithful. The turning-point theorem's F3 has the endpoint/positive-part notation collision recorded in alerts; its envelope restatement needs clarification.

Preserves norm versus strong-integral classes, mild versus common-domain conclusions, corrected amplitude pairing and finite-time errors. Adiabatic generators are scaled by H/ℏ with coherent followed projections.
The driven coherent-response example uses the current Weyl conjugations, phase S=∫fq/2 and invariant oscillator domain.
Distinguishes compact-support, dimensionless resolvent-tail and modified Coulomb comparisons; retains k>0, I+K inversion, threshold qualifications, amplitude constants and nonradial covariance.
The total-momentum lemma cites uniqueness of the arbitrary-Hilbert regular representing PVM, which the supplier proves under CC.
The mode-statistics example uses spectral uniqueness to identify its explicit free-energy multiplier PVM; it does not infer empirical statistics from this mathematics alone.
